documents.title: Refill Request — Ibuprofen
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called on lunch break for ibuprofen 600 refill. Uses it most days of her period plus a few other days a month, always with food. No stomach pain, no black stools. Still on the continuous pill. Refill sent per protocol, #60 with 2 refills. Gyn recheck is in April.

reports.text: Transvaginal ultrasound. Uterus retroverted, normal in size, homogeneous myometrium. Endometrium thin. Right ovary normal in size containing several small round cysts with homogeneous low-level internal echoes, the largest 1.8 cm, without internal vascularity. Left ovary normal in size with similar small cysts, the largest 1.4 cm, without internal vascularity. No solid component in either ovary. No hydrosalpinx. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Small bilateral ovarian cysts with the appearance of endometriomas ("chocolate cysts"), largest 1.8 cm on the right and 1.4 cm on the left.

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-Up — Endometriosis
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Date of visit: 04/13/2023

Follow-up of endometriosis (clinical diagnosis 10/2022) and bilateral tubal factor infertility. Seen by a different physician in the group today.

Despite six months more of the continuous pill and ibuprofen her pain has steadily worsened. Breakthrough bleeding every few weeks brings severe cramping, intercourse remains painful, and she describes missing work days and avoiding activities she used to enjoy. She and her husband still hope to have a child one day.

Meds: ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1/20 continuously, ibuprofen 600 mg prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: retroverted uterus; tenderness in the posterior cul-de-sac on bimanual; no palpable adnexal mass.

Labs today: hemoglobin 13.2, WBC 7.5, ESR 20, CA-125 58 (elevated).
Transvaginal ultrasound: several small cysts in both ovaries with the typical appearance of endometriomas.

Assessment: endometriosis with progressive pelvic pain on first-line suppression, now with small bilateral endometriomas and an elevated CA-125 that fits that picture.

Plan: diagnostic and operative laparoscopy to confirm the diagnosis, excise implants and free adhesions, and assess the tubes with dye. Consent discussed; she wants to schedule it for the end of the school year. Continue current medications until surgery.

OB/GYN

documents.title: Surgery
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My laparoscopy is booked for June 27, right after school lets out. Do I need a pre-op visit with you or bloodwork from your office?

documents.title: RE: Surgery
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: For a healthy person having an outpatient laparoscopy the surgical center's pre-admission team handles what's needed, and you're up to date with us. If they ask for a clearance letter, send me the form. Hoping this gives you some relief.

procedures.procedure: Laparoscopy with excision of endometriosis implants and lysis of pelvic adhesions

reports.text:
Specimens: (A) peritoneum, posterior cul-de-sac, excision; (B) pelvic peritoneum, right pelvic sidewall, excision.
Gross: A, two tan-red fibrous tissue fragments, 1.6 x 0.8 x 0.3 cm in aggregate. B, one tan fibrous fragment, 1.1 x 0.5 x 0.2 cm. Entirely submitted.
Microscopic: both specimens show endometrial-type glands with surrounding endometrial stroma within fibrotic peritoneal tissue, with hemosiderin-laden macrophages. No atypia. No malignancy.
reports.conclusion: A and B: endometriosis. Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Operative Report — Laparoscopy
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outpatient surgery center, gynecology
Date of surgery: 06/27/2023
Preoperative diagnosis: endometriosis, chronic pelvic pain, bilateral tubal factor infertility.
Postoperative diagnosis: same, confirmed; pelvic adhesions.
Procedure: diagnostic laparoscopy, excision of endometriosis implants, lysis of pelvic adhesions, chromopertubation.
Anesthesia: general. EBL minimal. Complications: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Findings: retroverted uterus of normal size. Endometriosis implants on the peritoneum of the posterior cul-de-sac and right pelvic sidewall. Both ovaries normal in size, each with small endometriomas, left in place to preserve ovarian reserve. Filmy adhesions around both tubes and adnexa. Upper abdomen normal.

Description: umbilical entry and two lower ports. Adhesions lysed sharply, freeing both adnexa. Implants excised with margins and sent to pathology. Chromopertubation with dilute indigo carmine after adhesiolysis: the right tube filled and spilled freely; the left tube did not fill. Hemostasis assured, ports closed.

Disposition: discharged home the same day.
Pathology: endometriosis in both specimens.
Follow-up: office in 6 weeks.

medications.drug_text: ethinyl estradiol 0.02 MG / norethindrone acetate 1 MG Oral Tablet
medications.reason: Stopped by gynecology after laparoscopy to allow conception

documents.title: Gynecology Post-Operative Visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Date of visit: 08/09/2023

Six weeks after laparoscopy with excision of endometriosis and adhesiolysis. Incisions healed. Pain much better than before surgery. Pathology confirmed endometriosis.

We reviewed that at surgery the right tube opened with dye after the adhesions were freed, while the left remained blocked. She and her husband would like to try to conceive on their own for now. We will stop the continuous pill today. Ibuprofen for period pain. If no pregnancy in 6 to 12 months, return to reproductive endocrinology.

Meds: ibuprofen 600 mg prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.
OB/GYN

orders.order: Return visit in 6 months, pelvic pain follow-up

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit, few days before teachers go back.

Interval: laparoscopy 6/27, endometriosis confirmed on pathology, implants excised, adhesions freed. Gyn op note says right tube open on dye, left still blocked. Post-op visit 8/9: off the continuous pill now, they're going to try on their own for 6-12 months, then back to REI if needed.

Feels like a different person. Pain 1/10 today, "the everyday ache is gone." First period off the pill came last week, crampy for a day, ibuprofen covered it. Intercourse comfortable again.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, ibuprofen 600 prn. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, cheerful. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, three small healed port scars, nontender.

A/P
1. Endometriosis s/p laparoscopic excision and adhesiolysis 6/2023, pain much improved. Off hormonal suppression to try to conceive. Ibuprofen prn. Med list updated.
2. Tubal factor infertility: per gyn, right tube patent after surgery. Continue prenatal.
3. Health maintenance: CBC/CMP. Flu and COVID this fall. Pap due next year.
Check in around February, sooner if pain returns.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count, kidney and liver tests from Tuesday are all normal. Have a good first week back.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pregnancy screen: LMP 10/3, pt reports no chance she's late. Flu vaccine L arm, 2023-24 Pfizer COVID R arm. VIS sheets given. Waited 15 minutes, fine.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Melissa, we missed you at your 3:40 appointment last Tuesday. Would you like to reschedule?

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So sorry!! Parent conferences ran over and I completely forgot. Honestly I'm doing well, periods are crampy the first day or two and the ibuprofen handles it, no pain otherwise. No pregnancy yet. Could I just see you at my physical instead of rescheduling?

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's fine, glad things are holding. See you at your physical. If the pain creeps back, or if you want to talk about going back to the fertility clinic, message me anytime.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax for ibuprofen 600 mg refill. Last filled 1/2024, using only around periods. Routed to PCP.

reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. HPV negative.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, after school this year since summer got away from her.

Interval: missed the February check, messaged instead. Endometriosis pain stays controlled after last year's surgery: first day or two of each period, ibuprofen helps, no pain between, intercourse fine. Cycles regular, 28 days. Not pregnant in the 14 months since surgery; they haven't gone back to REI and aren't sure they will. No new symptoms, no discharge, no fever.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, ibuprofen 600 prn. NKDA.
SH: never smoker, a glass of wine a week or so.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Thyroid normal size. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, port scars healed. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected, bimanual with retroverted uterus, nontender, no masses.

A/P
1. Endometriosis, quiet on ibuprofen alone.
2. Infertility: reminded her the REI door is open; she'll think about it.
3. Preventive: Pap/HPV today (5 years). STI screening today given her history: GC/chlamydia, HIV, RPR. Lipids and CBC. Flu and 2024-25 COVID today.
PHQ-2 1. Return 1 year.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 7 days

orders.order: Chlamydia and gonorrhea NAAT, retest in 3 months

documents.title: Result Call — Chlamydia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt on her lunch break re: positive chlamydia NAAT from Thursday's screen. Gonorrhea, HIV and syphilis negative. She has no symptoms. Upset but took it calmly.

Plan: doxycycline 100 mg BID x 7 days sent. Expedited partner therapy: second doxycycline prescription for her husband under his name per state EPT guidance. No intercourse until both have finished 7 days of treatment. Retest in 3 months. Call for fever or pelvic pain; with her history I want to hear early.
Pap from 10/10 still pending.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap and HPV test are normal. Next one in five years. The lab order for your recheck in January is in, just stop by any morning after the 13th.

documents.title: Other labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Did my cholesterol come back okay? And we both picked up the doxycycline Monday night.

documents.title: RE: Other labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, cholesterol and blood count are normal. Good that you both started. Take the doxycycline with a full glass of water and stay upright for 30 minutes after, and go easy on direct sun this week.
